'''Abdel Nader''' (born September 25, 1993) is an Egyptian [[basketball]] player who recently closed his college career with the [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State Cyclones]].

== Early life and high school career ==
Abdel averaged 23.8 points, 8.6 rebounds and 2.8 assists per game as a senior at [[Niles North High School|Niles North]] and led the [[Niles North High School|Vikings]] to a 24-6 record and their first sectional championship and [[Central Suburban League]] titles in the school’s 47-year history.  He garnered First Team All-State honors from the [[Chicago Tribune]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/highschool/ct-spt-0403-prep-bkb-all-state-first-20110402-htmlstory.html |title=Boys basketball: 2011 Chicago Tribune All-State first team: Connecticut Stanford Kentucky Louisville Ryan Boatright, Anthony Davis, Wayne Blackshear, Chasson Randle, Abdel Nader |publisher=Chicagotribune.com |date=2011-04-02 |accessdate=2015-06-25}}</ref> earned [[Chicago Sun-Times]] Class 4A Second Team All-State recognition, and named to the [[ESPN]] Chicago All-Area team.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/blog/chicago/high-school/post/_/id/994/boys-basketball-all-area-team-2009-10 |title=Boys basketball all-area team 2010-11 - Chicago High School Blog - ESPN |publisher=Espn.go.com |date=2011-03-17 |accessdate=2015-06-25}}</ref>

== College career ==
=== Freshman season ===
Nader appeared in all 31 games starting in 29 of them. He averaged a team-best 10.4 points, third among [[Mid-American Conference|MAC]] freshmen; and 4.2 rebounds, second-best among [[Mid-American Conference|MAC]] freshmen.  Nader recorded 21 steals and a team-high 22 blocked shots, the best among conference freshmen. He made his first collegiate start in the season opener at [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Purdue]], scoring nine points and grabbing four rebounds.  Abdel scored in double figures in 17 games, including three games of 20-plus points as well as having a season-best 26 points against [[Ball State Cardinals men's basketball|Ball State]].  Nader's impressive freshman season earned him [[Mid-American Conference|MAC]] All-Freshman Team honors.<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=http://www.niuhuskies.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030712aab.html |title=Nader Named to MAC All-Freshman Team - NIUHUSKIES.COM - The Northern Illinois Official Athletic Site |publisher=Niuhuskies.com |date=2012-03-07 |accessdate=2015-06-25}}</ref>

=== Sophomore season ===
Nader began the season as a preseason All-[[Mid-American Conference|MAC]] West selection.  He started 18 of the 19 games he played in, leading the team in scoring at 13.1 points while averaging 5.6 rebounds, 1.3 assists and shooting 77.2 percent from the free-throw line (44-57 FT). He scored in double figures 13 times, including three games with 20-plus points. Abdel posted 23 points on 4-of-5 shooting from 3-point range against [[Central Michigan Chippewas men's basketball|Central Michigan]] (8-12 FG).  He was named [[Mid-American Conference|MAC]] West Player of the Week on Feb. 4 after averaging 22.5 points and 11.0 rebounds during the week.<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=http://www.niuhuskies.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/020413aaa.html |title=Nader Named MAC West Player of the Week - NIUHUSKIES.COM - The Northern Illinois Official Athletic Site |publisher=Niuhuskies.com |date=2013-02-04 |accessdate=2015-06-25}}</ref>  At the end of the season, Nader decided he needed a fresh start and needed to transfer out of the program.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://collegebasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2013/03/28/report-northern-illinois-leading-scorer-abdel-nader-to-transfer/ |title=Report: Northern Illinois leading scorer Abdel Nader to transfer | CollegeBasketballTalk |publisher=Collegebasketballtalk.nbcsports.com |date= |accessdate=2015-06-25}}</ref>

=== Junior season ===
Nader eventually transferred to [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]].<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=http://amestrib.com/sections/sports/isu-cyclones/men%E2%80%99s-basketball-northern-illinois-transfer-nader-headed-isu.html |title=Men’s Basketball: Northern Illinois transfer Nader headed to ISU | Ames Tribune |publisher=Amestrib.com |date=2013-04-26 |accessdate=2015-06-25}}</ref>  He had to sit out the [[2013–14 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2013-2014]] season, becoming elibible again for the [[2014–15 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2014–15]] season.  He saw action in 32 games, averaging 5.8 points and 2.9 rebounds in 16.4 minutes per game. He was tied for second on the team with 16 blocked shots.  Abdel grabbed six boards, two blocks, two steals, and hit 6-of-10 field goals, including 4-of-6 behind the arc to score 19 points in [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State's]] annual victory at [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball|Iowa]].<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=http://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/college/iowa-state/basketball-mens/2014/12/12/cyhawk-showdown-adbel-nader-naz-long-aaron-white-carver-hawkeye-arena/20334251/ |title=Iowa State dismantles Hawkeyes in Cy-Hawk showdown |publisher=Desmoinesregister.com |date=2014-12-12 |accessdate=2015-06-25}}</ref> He matched his season-high with 19 points at [[West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball|West Virginia]].  Nader scored 11 points and had six rebounds at home against [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State]], he scored seven consecutive points in key second-half run against the [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Wildcats]] and blocked a fastbreak layup with 2:48 left that would have given the [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Wildcats]] the lead.<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=http://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/college/iowa-state/basketball-mens/2015/01/20/abdel-nader-iowa-state-basketball-cyclones-kansas-state-big-conference-hilton-coliseum/22087443/ |title=Abdel Nader's big block alters course of Iowa State's win |publisher=Desmoinesregister.com |date=2015-01-20 |accessdate=2015-06-25}}</ref>  Nader averaged 11.2 points and 5.3 rebounds when playing at least 20 minutes, ISU was 8-1 in those games.
